title: Given a Scenario, Troubleshoot Common Performance Issues

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: Performance troubleshooting turns 'the network is slow' into measurable symptoms: insufficient capacity, delay, loss, variation, or wireless instability.
bullets: Signal degradation, weak coverage, disassociation, and roaming problems
sections.callout: MEASURE CAPACITY → FIND DELAY → FIND LOSS → FIND VARIATION → CHECK WIRELESS

sections.title: Maestro Focus
paragraphs: Separate the performance metric from its possible cause. Bandwidth is potential capacity; throughput is what the application actually receives.
bullets: One constrained component limits the path → Bottleneck
Delay changes from packet to packet → Jitter

entries.title: Congestion and Contention
paragraphs: Congestion occurs when traffic demand exceeds available capacity. Contention occurs when multiple devices compete for a shared medium or resource.

entries.title: Bottlenecking
paragraphs: A bottleneck is the slowest or most constrained component in an end-to-end path. Faster components elsewhere cannot overcome it.
entries.memoryHook: The narrowest point controls the flow.

entries.title: Bandwidth
paragraphs: Bandwidth is the theoretical capacity of a link or channel.
entries.memoryHook: How much the pipe could carry.

entries.title: Throughput Capacity
paragraphs: Throughput is the useful data rate achieved in real conditions after protocol overhead, competition, loss, and device limits.
entries.memoryHook: How much data actually gets through.

entries.title: Latency
paragraphs: Latency is the time traffic takes to travel from source to destination. Distance, queuing, processing, and retransmissions can increase it.

entries.title: Packet Loss
paragraphs: Packet loss means traffic never reaches its destination. Congestion, errors, failing links, and wireless interference are common causes.

entries.title: Jitter
paragraphs: Jitter is variation in delay between packets. Voice and video are especially sensitive because playback expects a consistent arrival rhythm.

entries.title: Interference
paragraphs: Other wireless networks, non-Wi-Fi transmitters, microwave ovens, Bluetooth devices, and electrical equipment can corrupt or delay frames.

entries.title: Channel Overlap
paragraphs: Nearby access points on overlapping channels compete and interfere. Channel planning reduces this self-inflicted problem.

entries.title: Signal Degradation or Loss
paragraphs: Distance, walls, metal, absorption, reflection, and antenna placement weaken or distort the signal.
entries.memoryHook: The radio signal fades or is obstructed.

entries.title: Insufficient Wireless Coverage
paragraphs: Coverage gaps occur when access-point placement, transmit power, antenna choice, or density cannot adequately serve an area.
entries.memoryHook: No strong cell where the client needs one.

entries.title: Client Disassociation
paragraphs: A client repeatedly loses its association because of signal problems, interference, authentication failures, AP load, or configuration issues.
entries.memoryHook: The client falls off the WLAN.

entries.title: Roaming Misconfiguration
paragraphs: Poorly coordinated SSIDs, security settings, channels, thresholds, or controller policies can prevent smooth movement between access points.
entries.memoryHook: Movement between APs is the trigger.

sections.title: Recognition Cues
bullets: Devices compete for shared access → Contention
One slow component controls path → Bottleneck
Nearby WLAN frequencies collide → Channel overlap
Weak signal across distance/barriers → Signal loss
Failure while moving between APs → Roaming misconfiguration

entries.title: Congestion vs. Contention
paragraphs: Congestion is excess load on a path; contention is competition for shared access.

entries.title: Bottleneck vs. Congestion
paragraphs: A bottleneck is the limiting component; congestion is the overloaded condition that may occur there.

entries.title: Bandwidth vs. Throughput
paragraphs: Bandwidth is potential capacity; throughput is achieved data transfer.

entries.title: Latency vs. Packet Loss
paragraphs: Latency arrives late; packet loss does not arrive.

entries.title: Latency vs. Jitter
paragraphs: Latency is delay; jitter is variation in delay.

entries.title: Interference vs. Channel Overlap
paragraphs: Interference can come from many external sources; channel overlap specifically involves colliding Wi-Fi channel space.

entries.title: Signal Loss vs. Coverage
paragraphs: Signal loss describes weakening on the path; insufficient coverage describes an area without adequate service.

entries.title: Disassociation vs. Roaming
paragraphs: Disassociation is the client losing connection; roaming misconfiguration is specifically a handoff problem between APs.
